O1.business: Harbor Logistics runs 41 inland container terminals and a truck brokerage; it sells throughput to shippers and rail partners under 3 to 7 year take-or-pay contracts.
O1.how_it_makes_money: Terminal fees 58%, brokerage 27%, storage and chassis 15%.
O1.thesis_bull: Contracted volumes step up 9% in FY27 as two Gulf terminals open; pricing resets on 40% of the book; buybacks retire 4% of shares a year.
O1.thesis_bear: Brokerage margins compress when truck capacity loosens; Gulf ramp slips a quarter; leverage at 3.1x limits the buyback.
O1.valuation: 11.8x FY27 EBITDA against rails at 12.5x; the stock prices a flat brokerage margin and no Gulf upside.
O1.change_mind: Two quarters of lifts below +3%, or a Gulf opening pushed past Q2 FY27.

prints.event: Canada Consumer Price Index, September (Statistics Canada)
prints.read: Only matters to US futures through the energy pass-through read-across; a 3.2% headline with the BoC core still near 2.4% keeps the Bank of Canada on hold on October 28, while a hotter print would echo last week's US CPI and lean on the front end.

Builder sentiment is already deep in contraction after a three-point drop in September (present sales 35, expectations 37, traffic 23); another dip is expected with the 10-year above 5%, so only a print under 30 or a bounce back above 32 moves anything, and it is the only US release of the day.
No consensus found; bill stops read the front end's view of the October 28 meeting, and a 26-week stop staying well above the 13-week keeps the December hike priced.

prints.event: China GDP, third quarter (NBS, released Sunday evening CT)
prints.read: A small beat on the year-on-year rate with the quarter-on-quarter pace at 1.2%, enough to steady Asia and support US futures overnight but not a growth story on its own.
In line; factory output is holding up while property investment is down 20.6% year to date and the surveyed urban jobless rate sits at 5.2%.
The clearest beat of the batch, though a 1% consumer is still weak and investment is the drag.

prints.event: China fixed-asset investment, January to September (NBS)
prints.read: The miss in the batch; investment is contracting faster than expected with property down 20.6%, which caps how much the GDP beat helps commodities and industrial names.

read.call: A relief bounce led by the Nasdaq after Friday's AI-debt selloff, with oil off its Friday high and the 10-year easing to 5.07%, but a thin calendar and Fed blackout leave the tape hostage to Hormuz headlines and midweek tech earnings.
read.swing: Oil: Russia's foreign minister is in Tehran today and Iran's seven-day Hormuz proposal is still open, so a headline that pushes Brent back above $110 flips the call, while a credible reopening step extends the bounce.
drivers: Futures at 05:45 ET: Nasdaq 100 +1.0%, S&P 500 +0.5%, Dow flat, after the Nasdaq lost 4.5% on the week.
Oil: Brent $108.24 (-1.5%) and WTI $100.73 after Friday's $109.86 Brent settlement, the highest since May, as Trump waived some Russia sanctions and Vance talked de-escalation.
Rates: 10-year 5.07% at 03:38 ET, 24 bp under the October 5 closing high of 5.31% and well off the 5.33% spike after Wednesday's CPI.
Fed: blackout through October 29; October 28 priced 85% hold, December priced 76% for a hike to 4.00-4.25%.
US data today is only the NAHB index at 09:00 CT; the week builds to housing starts Tuesday, the 20-year auction Wednesday, claims Thursday, and flash PMIs Friday.

what_mattered.headline: Friday's AI-debt selloff ended the Nasdaq's four-week run
what_mattered.fact: S&P 500 closed 7,659.44 (-1.1% Friday, -1.9% on the week); Nasdaq 26,140.03 (-2.1%, -4.5% on the week); Dow 52,002.41 (-0.3%, +0.7% on the week); Russell 2000 2,721.37 (-1.7%). CoreWeave fell 12% Friday and 25% on the week on debt concerns; Micron -5.6%, Intel -5.8%.
what_mattered.implication: The leadership trade cracked on financing, not demand, so Wednesday's Meta, Tesla, IBM, Texas Instruments and Lam Research prints decide whether this is a rotation or the start of a drawdown.

what_mattered.headline: September CPI ran hot on gasoline, core nudged up
what_mattered.fact: Headline CPI +0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y (consensus 3.6%, prior 3.4%); core +0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y (consensus 0.2% and 2.5%); gasoline +9.1% m/m. PPI printed 6.3% y/y.
what_mattered.implication: Energy is doing the damage and core is grinding higher, which is why December hike odds sit near 76-89% even as October has faded to a hold.

what_mattered.headline: October hike odds collapsed to a hold, December stays live
what_mattered.fact: October 28 priced 85.1% for 3.75-4.00% and 14.9% for a hike; December 9 priced 76.0% for 4.00-4.25% and 13.0% for 4.25-4.50%. Late-October hike odds were 28% before Friday and near 33% after the CPI print.
what_mattered.implication: The front end has moved the hike to December, so this week's bill and 20-year auctions test whether the market will keep paying 5% for duration into a blackout week.

what_mattered.headline: Yields eased into the weekend despite the hot inflation data
what_mattered.fact: 10-year above 5.09% late Friday (+2 bp), down from a 5.33% spike after Wednesday's CPI; 5.07% early Monday. Gold futures $4,190 (+0.5%).
what_mattered.implication: Bonds caught a safety bid as equities sold off, so a stable 10-year near 5.05-5.10% is what the equity bounce needs today.

what_mattered.headline: Oil: Brent settled at a five-month high Friday, then slipped on a Russia sanctions waiver and de-escalation talk
what_mattered.fact: Brent settled $109.86 Friday (+3.7%, +4.9% on the week); WTI $101.41 (+10.4% on the week). Early Monday Brent $108.24 (-1.5%), WTI $100.73. Iran's seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal stays on the table; US Central Command says the blockade has redirected 138 vessels; Lavrov is due in Tehran Monday.
what_mattered.implication: Oil is the inflation channel the Fed cannot look through twice; Bessent called it an energy shock and said prices come down on the other side of the conflict, which the market is partly pricing this morning.

what_mattered.headline: China Q3 GDP beat by a tenth, investment missed
what_mattered.fact: GDP 4.5% y/y (consensus 4.4%), 1.2% q/q; industrial production 5.5% (consensus 5.4%); retail sales 1.1% (consensus 0.5%); fixed-asset investment -7.2% YTD (consensus -6.5%); property investment -20.6% YTD.
what_mattered.implication: Enough to steady Asia overnight, not enough to change the commodity demand picture while investment contracts.

look_at: Canada CPI at 07:30 CT: a 3.2% y/y headline is priced, so watch the m/m core at 0.2% and whether gasoline pass-through shows the same +9% monthly jump the US printed, the only inflation data before the US open.
Oil through the session: Lavrov in Tehran and the open seven-day Hormuz proposal mean one headline moves Brent $3 either way; Brent back above $110 reverses the futures bounce.
The 10-year around 5.07%: a close back above 5.10% while the Nasdaq bounces says the bounce is not trusted, a close under 5.05% confirms the safety bid is sticking.
AI credit names at the open: CoreWeave after a 25% week and the semiconductor ETF after a 4% Friday drop tell you whether the financing scare is spent before Wednesday's Meta and Tesla prints.
Bill auction stops at 10:30 CT and GDPNow tomorrow at 10:00 CT (last 3.6% on October 15): a 26-week stop above 4.20% keeps December at 76% and a GDPNow upgrade adds to it.

fed.market_pricing: October 28: 85.1% hold at 3.75-4.00%, 14.9% hike to 4.00-4.25%; December 9: 76.0% hike to 4.00-4.25%, 13.0% to 4.25-4.50%, 11.0% unchanged (investing.com Fed rate monitor, October 19 morning). FedWatch secondary reports October 16-18 put the hold at 84.5-87.3%.
speakers_today: None scheduled: the pre-FOMC blackout runs October 17 through October 29 and the Board calendar lists only statistical releases (commercial paper 12:00 CT, H.10 and H.15 at 15:15 CT).

themes: The Fed hike has moved from October to December: October 28 odds fell from roughly 33% after Wednesday's CPI to 15% by Friday, while December holds near 76-89%, so the blackout week is about whether 5% duration clears without a Fed voice.
AI financing replaced AI demand as the tech debate: CoreWeave lost 25% on the week and the Nasdaq 4.5%, and Wednesday's Meta and Tesla capex commentary is the test.

Oil at a five-month high ($109.86 Brent) is now the inflation driver, not shelter: gasoline added half of September's 0.6% CPI gain, and the Hormuz proposal plus the Russia sanctions waiver are the two paths back under $100.
